utterances.text: Here there's mention of certain places. Do you remember this? And, in particular, what do these figures tell you, especially the sentence preceding the list of these numbers?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The army of the Bosnia-Herzegovina 1st Corps command, strictly confidential." This is submitted to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and General Staff Karkin. It's an entering combat report 8-0, 330 hours [as interpreted]. On the morning of the 5th of May, 1995, we received an entering combat report from the forward command post of the 14th Division, Bijela Lijeska, which we are transmitting in its entirety. From 0930 hours, the Chetniks directed heavy artillery and mortar fire on the Djokin Toranj, trig point 2086, firing around 1.000 shells. At around 1930, the Chetniks seized Djokin Toranj. During the night work was being done to establish a new line of defence which we held before Djokin Toranj was seized. Since we have used up around 1.000 shells and grenades over the past four days, we need the following replenishment: 60-millimetre shell --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We see the list. What can you tell us? What actually happened here with this Djokin Toranj?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Djokin Toranj is at the linkup point here between the Herzegovina Corps and the corps in the area of responsibility of the Herzegovina Corps. This is the linkup point between the two corps of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who took this location first?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st and the 4th Corps of BH seized these positions in a concerted action.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was the conflict about?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conflict was about who was going to take full control of this small feature. That's a hill on Treskavica called Djokin Toranj.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we also please have this document admit as a Defence exhibit, because it shows the commencement of the may conflicts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D188, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now look a document DD00-1747.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I please have it enlarge it a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, here, I have only a portion of this document translated, and I would like to put it to witness. If he can first look on page 1, whose document this is, and then I'm going to ask him about the portion that was translated because I had to arrange for a translation myself. Oh, yes, yes. We did receive the whole translation. Now we have it on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So who issued this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st Corps command of the BH army issued this document on the 16th of May, 1995. That's mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can this preamble indicate where these conflicts took place? Please slow down. Wait for me to finish my question before you give me an answer. Look at it, and then tell me where these clashes broke out.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These clashes broke out in the Zlatiste, Debelo Brdo, Trebevic, and Spicasta Stijena sectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is this area here: Debolo Brdo, Zlatiste, Trebevic, and Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now move to page one, which speaks about the daily use or expenditure of ammunition on the 16th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is, Your Honour, when the indictment incidents took place, among other things. If we can please look at page 2; chapter entitled "Consumption of Ammunition." Do you see this? Does this show the amount of the ammunition spent by the 12th Division.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since this was the area of responsibility of the 12th Division, and that comprised the town area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you give us a few figures?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Large calibre: 120-millimetre mortar, 76 shells; 82-millimetre mortar, 466 pieces; 60-millimetre mortar, 379 shell; B1 gun shells, 10; and now come to infantry ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What's the number of rounds?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16.300, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we have this document please admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. But what are we to make of the evidence about the ammunition? Are you saying this is at a very high level or exactly what do you want us to draw from this evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to draw your attention to the fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that in May only 16.000 rounds of bullets were fired, and that was at the time, when, according to the indictment, a large number of incidents took place, and this is also a time when an ongoing conflict began, which went all through June and July in particular. Through some other documents, you will be able to see that on a daily basis thousands and thousands of rounds of bullets and shells were fired from the 12th Division positions. This is the period May, June, July, all the way through the period when into NATO bombing started. This kind of fire came on a daily basis from the area of responsibility of the 12th Division. This document demonstrates that on the 15th of May, or rather, 16th of May, so many shells were fired, 76 of 120 millimetre, and so on and so forth, and also 16.000 rounds of ammunition. I think this is particularly relevant for this period because this shows that an activity, combat activity was being launched that went on permanently and that it was particularly pursued by the BH army. Because if the Defence is not availed of an opportunity to show what the situation was in the course of this clash in the aftermath of the truth, then I think that the Defence will be really put in a position not to address this whole issue in a just and fair way, the issue that relates and pertains to the indictment. The Defence believes that we have to demonstrate what kind of armed conflict took place in the period -- in this period. Of course, it does not justify any retaliatory actions, but we have to establish what kind of operations were ongoing. Even this rifle fire could have caused these incidents in a certain way. We already spoke about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. But bear in mind that the Prosecution's case, as I understand it, is not that combat activities were not engaged in or perhaps even initiated by the BH army. Their case is that there was activity on the part of the Serb forces, and that activity was carried out under the command of the accused and gave rise to the charges in the indictment of terror, war crimes, and crimes against humanity. They're not saying, as I understand it, that the BH army was inactive; in fact, I believe they concede that there was an armed conflict. That's the basis. That's one of the requirements for an indictment of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, nowhere in the indictment did they establish the existence of an armed conflict. This was a free interpretation, but you will find nowhere in the indictment that there was an armed conflict involving two armies and, in particular, an armed conflict in the aftermath of the truce. When every day and I have numerous numbers of these reports because the Defence had an opportunity to see the files of BH army which was not the case notice Galic case, but I brought only the most illustrative ones because I'm sure that you wouldn't allow me more. I have, therefore, seven or eight reports of this kind that show what kind of conflict was going on in May, June, and July, and then until the end of the war, not to mention the NATO bombing. Under such circumstances, I believe that this whole matter has to be taken into consideration. There was truce, first, then what followed was the phase that we described; and now, since there is mention about the campaign, not only whether a certain number of incidents took place, which we're going to examine whether they were proved or not, in which the accused is charged with direct involvement. However, here we have a phase in this armed conflict which was dominated by fire from all kinds of weapons predominantly from the positions of BH army and the area of responsibility of their 1st Corps. Therefore, I believe that the Defence indeed should be allowed to demonstrate this in evidence, not only through telling stories, but also to prove this by presenting documents retrieved and acquired from the BH archives. All this was happening concurrently with the incidents that the accused Milosevic is charged with in May and June, and I think this is relevant and the Defence should be allowed to take this course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, I'm not clear what your case is in relation to the existence or non-existence of an armed conflict. Would you clarify that for me? What are you saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I spoke at length and I thought that I would not have to go into explaining this again, when we discussed the campaign to instill terror, for instance. I simply fail to understand why I have to explain those arguments yet again, because if we're talking about fear, terror, and a campaign to instill it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have to explain because the Chamber needs the clarification. It's the duty of the Trial Chamber to keep abreast of the arguments presented by counsel in this case and to ensure that it understands the arguments that are being presented, and that's why you are asked to explain it. So, once again --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, please do not deduce on basis on of my silence that I do not know the answer. But if the Defence has not managed to show what we intend to prove in our case, and if such documents and the evidence of this sort cannot be used to clarify the issues regarding, in particular, this period that the dominant period that is in fact half of the period relevant for the indictment against General Milosevic in which the most blatant incidents occurred, the bombs, the shells --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you not hear the question I asked you? It's quite simple. I'm asking to you explain to me what is your position; that is, the position of the Defence in relation to the issue of an armed conflict? And I ask it specifically because in the last intervention from you, which was very long, you started out by saying that the Prosecution either did not allege the existence of an armed conflict or did not sufficiently prove it, yet at the end of your intervention you referred to an armed conflict. So I'm confused as to what your position is, and that's what I'm asking to you do, to explain to me what the position of the Defence is with regard to this issue. Concentrate on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence contends that there was not a conflict, in the broader significance of the word, in the entire former Yugoslavia, but that there was an armed conflict on very specific demarcation lines, and this is not stated in the indictment at all. The BH army is not mentioned at all. It is as if it had not existed. And if we are not allow to prove in what ways the BH army actually operated in this area, what the front line looked like, what was happening at the demarcation lines at the time when the incidents took place in the times relevant in the indictment, then I simply I cannot see why I have to explain this at any greater length or in any greater detail. I'm trying to prove that on any given day, thousands and thousands, hundreds of hundreds of shells were fired from the 1st Corps positions, the BH army 1st Corps positions, and that the primary goal was simply something that had to do with the protection of living on one side. No reprisals, no retaliation, but just response to operations launched by the other side in June, July, August, September, October, November when the incidents listed in the indictment actually took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that intervention. First, paragraph 26 of the indictment reads: "At all material times relevant to this indictment, an armed conflict existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the territory of the former Yugoslavia." In the light of that, I don't understand your contention that the Prosecution does not allege an armed conflict or that no evidence has been brought in relation to that issue. Now, secondly, you say what you are trying to prove that "on any given day, thousands and thousands, and I'm reading from the transcript, hundreds of hundreds of shells were fired from the 1st Corps positions, the BH army 1st Corps positions, and that the primary goal was simply something that had to do with the protection of living on one side. No reprisals,, no retaliation just response to operations launched by the other side in June, July, August, September, October, November when the incidents listed in the indictment actually took place." You're going to bring evidence that will show, as I understand it, then, that in relation to the allegations in the indictment in those months, the BH army was simply responding to attacks launched -- sorry, that the Serb army was simply responding to attacks launched by the BH army. Because if you're going to do that, then, of course, that would be very, very relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, is it possible, Your Honour, I explained all this in my opening statement. Everything that was done in this time-period in light of the specific situation was done in extreme necessity, in extreme military necessity in this type period. On other occasions, again, we had a necessity; but in this period, everything was done in extreme military necessity in order to prevent the other side from achieving military goals. I explained this in my opening statement, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Tapuskovic, I hear what you have said, and I am very have interested in it. Now, when you bring that evidence later on, when you call your witnesses, my advise to is that you must as far as possible relate that evidence to the allegations in the indictment. Don't allow the evidence to be at large. Let it be related as specifically as possible to the allegations in the indictment, and that way you will show or attempt to show that the Serb forces were, as you have just told me, simply responding to attacks to protect themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And may I add, Mr. Tapuskovic, that the difficulty we have is to conclude from the evidence that you have shown to us in these orders to conclude that the fire exchanged between the two parties was just from the Serb side being responsive to attacks from the ABiH side. And the difficulty we have, to be specific, is that we cannot conclude that from this evidence, because this evidence shows nothing more than the fact that there was fire. It doesn't show anything about who initiated the fire. So in continuation of the President's advice to you, I also strongly invite you to be more specific when you put the evidence to us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps it is important to stress this suggestion that I received, and that is that the Defence intends to prove, if it can, that a civilian person, and a civilian facility in particular in this period, that such persons and such facilities were never targeted by Republika Srpska army troops and that everything that happened, in particular in this time-period from October, or rather, August, 1994 until early May, that there were no such elements that pertain to what we were talking about as regards the campaign. But in this time-period, when the majority of the incidents occurred, that is in May and June, it is out of the question to claim that the Republika Srpska army targeted civilian persons or facilities at all. Your Honour, I cannot bring here witnesses to speak about the incidents because we cannot find such witnesses, and I cannot ask Witness Veljovic specifically about some incidents that took place in May, but I can adduce evidence to show what the situation looked like at the time. Based on some judgements that I read, it is not important who started the conflict at all. But in this time-period, the Defence contends and believes that it has irrefutable evidence that what happened in May, June, and July, and onwards, it is quite clear and it is well known who prepared the offensive an and who carried it out in this manner. And this is important for new your deliberations on who is responsible for the specific incidents, and we have yet to determine which of these incidents are the result of direct targeting and which incidents are a mere consequence of combat activities of fighting. Because it is quite natural that if you have fighting of this nature, you will have civilian casualties on both sides. And if I were to be allowed to try and prove, and this is out of the question, to prove that as many people were killed on the other side, 2.500 soldiers were killed on the other side. How were they killed? And hundreds of civilians were killed. How? Well, they were not targeted directly. I cannot credit that contention. But the armed conflict in Sarajevo is not -- I'm interested in the armed conflict in Sarajevo which was at the very heart, at the very core of the conflict in the broader region in the whole of our unfortunate country of the former Yugoslavia, and it affected all the peoples that took part in this conflict there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, thank you. Please continue now with the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, document DD00-1747 will be admitted as D189.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did I say so? I did? Well, if I did, that's all right. It is to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps I will brother you with all of these documents through some other witness. But at least for one point in time when the majority of the incidents occurred, according to the indictment, I would like to ask this witness what he can confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did you know? What did you learn about the participation of various divisions in the military operation that was being prepared, and when did this operation actually begin?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of May, 1995, and this can be seen from some documents, because I was able to obtain certain documents where I read some reports that were also published in the book by lye Rasim Delic. On the 18th of May, Army General Rasim Delic received an order from President Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Please, don't tell us about what you learned from the book. The Court is not interested in that. What I want to know is what reports did you receive about this offensive that was in the making at the time, and were you informed about what was about to happen?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were notified by our security and intelligence organ that is charged with the collecting of this kind of data, that on the 15th of June, at the latest, an offensive would be launched. The code-name was Operation T-95.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did this operation in fact begin?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It began at 3 hours, ten minutes on the 15th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know who took part in this offensive?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The offensive was carried out at the level of the BH army. The main agent was the 1st Corps. They were entrusted with carrying out combat activities. The attacks of the BH army, from the 18th of May until the 15th of June, used up all personnel, all the equipment, all the materiel, with the exception of the 5th Corps which was stationed in Bihac and the 81st division which was stationed in the Gorazde area, because they were in the UN-protected areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this knowledge of yours correspond to this document, DD00-1769?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think the witness is waiting to answer. Are you in a position to answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. "The army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the command of the 1st Corps, strictly confidential, 01/3-120. The date is the 6th -- the 8th of June, 1995. Order of the commander of the 1st Corps for attack."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 4, please. The English version is also page 4, and also in B/C/S page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see what it says here under number 4? Now what is written here, does that correspond fully to what it was that was happening at the separation line?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but pay attention to paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The commander of the corps decided in coordinated action with the forces of the 4th Corps, 3rd Corps, and 7th corps unit the of the Republic of BH, MUP, and with own support carry out a combined assault operation of the joint units of the 1st Corps with a simultaneous attack by the forces from the front of the zone of the 14th and 16th Divisions. 14th Division, 14th Division, the 16th Division, the forces of the 12th Division from Sarajevo the city area, and forces tactically infiltrated deep mind enemy lines," that is to say, in our territory. "Group the main forces in the zone of responsibility of the 14th Division along the Vijenac, trig point 1360; Crni Vrh, trig point 1788 axis; and the auxiliary forces in the zone of responsibility of the 16th Division and the 12th Division. Objective of operation: Break up the enemy forces." We are the enemy. "Along the axis of attack and take control of the Trnovo-Kijevo-Krupac road and the Semizovac-Srednje-Nisici road. With a part of the forces of the 12th Division, push the enemy between the Bosna river and Vogosca, and then link up with the forces of the 7th Corps in the Dvor village and Doboj village sector. Keep the thrust of artillery support, POB and PVO, on the axis of the attack of the main forces in the 12th Division."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that the way it was then? Was that it was at all the separation lines --

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: -- that were shown on the maps?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So what did this look like in relation to what was going on?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that we were following the activities of the 1st Corps and the operations, there was a change of -- in the main attack of the forces where the 7th Corps of General Mehmed Alagic is earmarked to be involved in the main attack and to look at the area of Bosna and Ilijas. Already on the 3rd of May, three brigades were brought into the area of Viseko, or rather, the village of Mostra and deployed to the village of Mostra --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. And what happened at the separation lines, for example, towards Grbavica, Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At ten past 3.00, at the same time, we were attacked simultaneously along the front line. The fiercest attacks were from Viseko and Kaluk towards Vogosca, and then from the area of Zuc here towards Semizovac; whereas, part of the 3rd Corps in the Nisica river valley was attacking, and their main objective was to cut off and encircle the population and the units here in this part of the front; and then from town towards this southern part from the direction of Debelo Brdo, they cut off our lifeline. Here, in the area of Zlatiste, they took up the roads; and then here in the area of Hrese, they broke through the positions; and then from the area of Mojmilo, they want towards the barracks in the area in Lukavica with a view to having the forces of the corps and the population thrown back to the plateau in Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In that first clash, were there any casualties?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces involved in the operation, and the operation was called Operation T-95, 61.5 per cent of the total potential of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was involved in this operation, vis-a-vis the corps. And in terms of numbers, this is between 130 to 135.000 men, and all of this against a corps that had 18.000 members. At first, we did not have any reinforcements; but later on, we got about 1.500 men to support us. Terrible losses were sustained, especially at the northern front. In five days, we had about 140 soldiers dead and tens of civilians killed and about 700 wounded, some of them seriously, some of them with light wounds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What period was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was notice period between the 15th of June, up until the 21st of June; that is to say, four, five, six days, we had these intensive attacks at the northern part of the front. Also in the southern part of the front, there were major losses as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to take this as an example that you just told us of a particular combat operation in which the Serb forces were outnumbered by the ABiH forces and suffered significant losses. So, Mr. Tapuskovic, how does that impact on any of the counts in the indictment? How are we to use that evidence? And I stress again that it is my duty, it is the duty of the Trial Chamber, to understand the case being presented by both sides. How are we to use that evidence in relation to, say, Count 1, which charges terror; or Counts 2 to 4 that charge sniping, murder, inhuman attacks, unlawful attacks on civilians; Counts 5 to 7, shelling, murder, inhuman attacks, unlawful attacks on civilians? You have evidence there now. We have evidence from this witness of this combat operation that took place as he said between - when is it, June? - the 15th and the 21st of June, in which the Serb force, were outnumbered and suffered significant losses. How are we to relate that to the charges in the indictment? What are you asking us to draw from that evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he did not say that this offensive lasted between the 15th and the 26th. He said that during these five or six days, there were losses, and he said how big the losses were. They are part of the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Never mind, that's not the important point. The point is that you have evidence. You're presenting evidence of a combat operation in which the Serb forces were outnumbered, probably even attacked by the ABiH, and suffered significant losses. And I'm asking what are you asking the Trial Chamber to draw from that in relation to the charges in the indictment? And could you point me specifically to any of the charges in which you would be asking us to say, for example, this evidence contradicts the allegation in the indictment or the evidence presented by the Prosecution in its case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you look at shelling, please look at the 16th of June. As for the 16th of June, there are a large number of incidents: Those that remained in the indictment and those that were in the original indictment; that is to say, that a large number of incompetences occurred on the 16th. I asked him about this offensive. And as for all the documents that I had -- from all the documents I had, I just singled out for the 16th, for that offensive, four or five documents that I have here; and that show from all brigades of the 12th Division, there was an abundance of shells of all kinds coming from there, and also there was rifle gun-fire as well. I wanted to show on the basis of a few document.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to show -- on the basis of a few documents, I wanted to show the Trial Chamber how big this activity was on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please, I didn't see Mr. Waespi on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I have been silent for a while. Just a couple of points, if I may on this issue. Because as you rightly observed, Your Honours, responding by the SRK to ABiH attacks or defensive actions, whatever you want to characterise, doesn't entitle the SRK to target civilians. Even if it was out of necessity, even that would not be a defence. And also not using air bombs. Three's three incidents mentioned on the 16th of June, incident 11, 12, and 13, as we know, there's been testimony, lots of testimony about the indiscriminate nature of these air bombs. It doesn't allow them to indiscriminately to shell the city in response where civilians are located, and we have seen casualties, where UNPROFOR members testified. Or the second argument I wanted to make, Mr. President, two days later, 18th June 1995, and this is our shelling incident number 14, the attack on the school of Dobrinja. We heard testimony saying that it was quiet on that day, so there was not even a response to anything. But even if it were the SRK, the accused is not allowed to target civilians, not even in response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Waespi. Of course, it's not my wish to anticipate the closing arguments in the case. I simply want and I think I'm obliged to try to understand the case that is being presented, and that's why I asked you to relate it to the indictment. You have referred us to the 16th of June in relation to which there are three incidents, and perhaps you might in the break look at the incidents referred to for the 16th of June. There are three. Mr. Waespi just referred to one on the 18th as well. But I'm grateful for the answer that you're giving me, and I believe that my understanding is developing as the case progresses. And I stress that I understand that that is part of my function. Let us take the break now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would first like to tender the document DD00-1769 to be admitted as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D190, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this again has to do with the discussion that we had before the break. I did my best to choose among the abundance of documents that I had in my hands those pertaining to what we discussed, i.e., the 16th of June. I refrain from obtaining any documents or showing them to the witness that pertain to any other date. I just wanted to show the situation prevailing on the 16th of June. I would first like to ask the witness about the actions that took place on the 16th of June, because Mr. Waespi mentioned another date; that is, the 18th of June and the school in Dobrinja, as well as some other things. These are the issues that we still have to discuss here in front of you, under which circumstances these incidents happened and who was responsible for the 18th of June, let alone the issue of air bombs. But I am kindly asking you to allow me to ask the witness, given what was happening on the 16th of June, as an example, if he can tell us some of the documents, and I will not deal with many other documents. However, I would like to single out the 16th of June. Will you allow me that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljovic, you said that when the conflict began, the one that took place on the 16th of June. How many actions or operations were on that date? Was there any significant for you to remember that date in terms of the number of operations under taken?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation started on the 15th, and as the day progressed they became more intense. One of the worst days was the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honours, in relation to this specific date, I would like to show the witness four documents showing the consumption of ammunition by the BH army and ask him to confirm whether this corresponded to what happened on that day. I would not tackle any other documents that I probably can tender in a different way. Can he tell me anything about the actions taken by the brigades of the 12th Division and whether that corresponds to the events of the 16th. For example, if we can look at the first document bearing this date, and there's a total of four of them, and with this we shall finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document and tell me something about document DD00-3583.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, that's not the best way to lead evidence. There's a document in front of the witness. Ask the witness a specific question about it. Don't ask him to give evidence at large, to tell you something about it. What is that you wish to hear? Elicit the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to hear from you Witness, Mr. Veljovic, about this date and the activities that took place. What weaponry was used, to what extent, and what kind of weapons?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th Division launched a fierce attack on the 16th, since due to some justifiable reasons it was unable to join other divisions on the 15th. It operated from the town concentrating --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the names of the locations. He was turned away from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, would you please repeat the names of the locations, as the interpreter didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 12th Division launched a fierce operation on the 16th from the inner town because that was its area of responsibility. The main axis of attack were from Zuc towards Vogosca, from Debelo Brdo to Zlatiste where they broke through the line. On both Zuc and Zlatiste, they cut off the communication and thereby encircled Grbavica all together. Then in the area of Falitici [phoen], they also broke through the defence lines, and this is where fierce fighting took place. The consumption of ammunition was at a very high level from all available weaponry such as mortars, guns, tanks, et cetera. They used it in order to cut off from Mojmilo towards the barrack, this area, and to encircle through Zlatiste and Mojmilo, and to link up in the area of Vogosca down the river of Misoca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: My question in relation to everything you mentioned and the operation in which all kinds of weaponry was used, and if I am allowed to show these four document, does the quantity of the materiel used and the weapons and the number of shells fired correspond to what happened on that day? That is why I'm showing you this document first, and just to look at the consumption on that day and which brigade it was.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was 111th Brigade, and it shows high level of consumption of ammunition, and a division is made up of several brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look specifically at the quantities of the materiel used on page 2 of the B/C/S version, because we have a translation of only this part.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it says that high-calibre rounds: Shells 60, 200; shell 82, 175; shell 120, 82; and 20.000 rounds of 762 bullets; 2.000, 7.2 depending on the calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did this correspond form what was coming from that direction?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document please be admitted as a Defence exhibit. I would like to show the witness only three other documents and then I leave it, and all of this refers to the 16th of June. This particular document refers to the 111th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes D191.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The same thing, only now it's document DD00-3588, bearing the same date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look which brigade we are talking about now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What date?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does this correspond to the quantity of ammunition shown on second page in the B/C/S version. Just a moment, please. Please look close to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Does this quantity correspond?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately. I didn't count each one. For example, 246, 60-millimetre shells; 41, 120-millimetre; 20-millimetre grenades, 120; et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be admitted as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we do so, maybe, Mr. Tapuskovic, you would like to explain to the Chamber what sort of ammunition is it that we see here on this and the preceding exhibit. I see, for instance, that 44 mines for RPG SADP were used. Could you clarify that a bit, what that is? I guess RPG stands for rocket propelled grenades. Do you use mines for this kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a hand-held anti-armour launcher used for destroying bunkers and armoured vehicles, but it can also destroy personnel inside; whereas, other munitions target only personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification. What is the Zolja of which four have been used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zolja is also an anti-armour weapon. It's calibre is 60 millimetres, and it is used also for destroying fortified munitions. There are others called Osa. It has a larger calibre and more power.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also tender this document to be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D192, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In order to shorten my examination, let us look at another document, which is DD00-35800. Which brigade is this and what is the date?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we just scroll it down a bit? I don't see. It's the 112th Brigade of the 12th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the same applies, approximately, to what you said about the previous document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I just have a clearer picture? I don't see very well. Can you improve the image?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning this document, can you tell us what is 7.9 calibre?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7.9 millimetre refers to a rifle bullet, just as 7.62 is for an automatic rifle. Those were the rifles manufactured in Zastava, and they were a bit old-fashioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we also have this document admitted as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D193, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know for how long you're going to tolerate me. It seems to me that the eight hours that I had asked for, I would like to know how long I have left. It seems to me that I have spent about four hours, and I think that I should be careful about this. You haven't made a decision, so I don't know exactly whether I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You don't wish to follow the practices of the Prosecutor then, because they simply went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, not all the time. I think we got into a habit of asking leave to ask a few questions. I don't have any objection for the Defence to use more time. It's the Defence's first witness, and that's our position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So how much more time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To tell you the truth, it's difficult for me to say, but I will take into consideration whatever the Chamber advises me to do. I will do my best to finish this by the end of business today or maybe earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Tapuskovic. We'll work on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very grateful to you, Your Honours. I will relax a bit now. I would like the witness to be shown document P665, please. 665, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljovic, please, with regard to this document, I have a few things that I would kindly ask you to read carefully before you give me answers. First, can you tell me who produced this document?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps from the forward command post at the Niksic plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you say what was the date?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 10th of August, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, you have already spoke about this, but can you please explain to the Judges once again. I think this will not be repetitive. Could you read the first paragraph, and tell us where those positions were?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since at this time I was in the 1st Romanija Brigade, which half of it was deployed in the Niksic plateau sector, I'm quite familiar with this. We're talking about October 1994 when the BH army units, from the Supreme Command staff of the BH army, when the Supreme Command staff of the BH army made the decision to launch a decisive attack to take the route Semizovac-Srednje-Nisici, and to cut off the supply lines for our equipment, materiel food for the forces deployed at the Niksic plateau, and we would effectively be cut off had they succeeded in doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You have spoke been that, so this is quite enough. Can you now please look at item 2 in this order; in fact, that would be item 1, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1, paragraph 2. "The Ilijas Infantry Brigade, the task is to first mount a persistent defence of current positions. Part of forces is to is extricate and attack along the route Tarcin-Dol-Krst, topographic point 1147, the village of Nasici, with a task of taking control of the Misoca river crossing and cutting off part of the enemy forces in this area supported by Corps Artillery Group 1."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show us on this map where those positions are, and can you just describe it very briefly.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are the positions right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what is this then?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they're attacking from this axis, the route, the communication route, and the forces that are in contact here have to mount a persistent defence. So their commander tasked with them with mounting a persistent defence and to extricate a part of the forces to attack and in order to prevent the enemy from cutting off that route.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So who is in an encirclement here, and who has an advantage here.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in -- with regard to the strength and with regard to the fact that they have the dominating position, this area was not really all that densely inhabited.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at item 5 on the next page in the B/C/S version. This is the 10th of August, 1994, and could you please look at item 5. That's page 2.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, item 5. Do you see it, and could you please read what it says in paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Colonel Cvetkovic is to group" --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says: "A launcher is to be prepared for operation in Mosevicko Brdo. AB," that probably means aerial bomb launcher, "is to be prepared for action, and another launcher is to be prepared to target Gradina, Konjsko Brdo, and Velika Bukovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, in your brigade, did you ever have the equipment that is listed here?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was in the 1st Romanija Brigade at the time, and 1st Romanija Brigade did not have any aerial bomb -- air bomb launchers as indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the information listed here, you read out Gradina, Konjsko - please wait until I finish - Konjsko Brdo, Velika Bukovo. You said that this is a rugged terrain, no roads leading in or out. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a wooded area, rugged terrain, impassable, and there are -- there is no population there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you, yourself, did you hear any reports from other fighters from other brigades about those air bombs?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I heard that some soldiers and some craftsmen were working on some makeshift launchers, and this actually had not been done properly at all. You need to have a plane in order to drop an air bomb. And if you don't comply with the instructions for use for -- with the manual, then you're not doing it properly, and you're incurring risk. I know that in one incident, six of our soldiers were killed in this sector. This was imprecise -- an imprecise weapon, and technically it was not perfected at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Does that mean -- well, I shouldn't really be leading you on this. If six soldiers were killed, as you say, whose soldiers?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, did you perhaps hear what was the reason or in fact what was done about it?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I often heard the commanders say that this weapon should not be used because of our safety, because it was not technically perfected.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of this document, what can we conclude, when was this?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in 1994, in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is a Prosecution Exhibit. It is already in evidence. Well, I would like to -- I would like us to look at Prosecution Exhibit 194. I hope that we will have time to deal with it. But while --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. There's something that I don't really understand regarding the exhibit that we have just seen. The witness is saying that what is written in this document is exact or not? This is what I'd like to know. This brigade of the Romanija Corps, it did have air bombs and launchers, yes or no? That's what I like to understand. Did the brigade have those launchers and air bombs or not. We could ask the witness, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, well, the witness replied that his brigade did not have any but that he heard, as he recounted to us. That's why I ask him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Your brigade, the brigade where you were serving,, did it at any point use such bombs.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While Milosevic was the commander and followed by Colonel Lizdek, we never had any such launchers. I heard that a 3rd Brigade had such launcher, and that the Ilijas Brigade and the Igman Brigade that they had. In fact, the troops, some craftsmen, did all kinds of makeshift weapons, including those launchers. This was very, very dangerous because it had not perfected before it was put to use. It was very imprecise. Nobody dared to even get close to those launchers; and once it was fired, it could easily fall on our own positions or villages. I think that there was a court case Because of the use of this weapon, and that was -- proceedings were launched by the prosecution office of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was there in Vogosca. They were testing this equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So this weapon was the way you just described it.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but this Prosecution document, it's true in the description of these launchers, you're not contesting the fact that these launchers did exist?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as you can see, the document that this witness spoke about clearly states that such a thing did exist and that it worked just as he described it in August 1994. So I wouldn't embark on making any further comments regarding the allegations in the indictment that all of a sudden this weapon was created and started being used in 1995, and it was designed to put an end to the conflict. We will in fact continue discussing this issue of air bombs as our case develops, but this is the document that I now showed to the witness and the witness knows what is the situation was at this time. He knows that it was used on the basis of what he heard. He knew that it was ready to be used in the rugged terrain uninhabited area, impassable terrain. That's what he explained. That's what I asked him and he gave me his answer. He told me that -- that because of all this hulabaloo, our people got killed. In one incident six people were killed. He heard about that, when one of those bombs was actually launched.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But now, since we have this map here in front of us, could you please now explain. Perhaps we could zoom in by zone and you know how to read a map, of course. Could you please tell us what does this map show in the area of responsibility of 101st Brigade, and we just heard that on one day, it fired the number -- certain number of shells as indicated in the document. So what do we see here? What do we see here? What does it have in terms of weapons?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we see here --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't see it here, but let's talk about 102nd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well the 102nd Brigade has a mortar platoon. It has launchers, as indicated by those arrows symbols. It has 60-millimetre mortars deployed here in behind the Mojmilo hill and on the Mojmilo hill sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And if we are look at 101st, if we go right on this map, what do those arrows signify?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are anti-armour and anti-fortification launchers. This is where you actually launch those anti-armour rockets that you use to fight armour and to destroy fortified facilities such as other bunkers or other buildings. And here behind the hill, in the inhabited area where you have the little dot with the half circle --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Veljovic, could you please take it slowly so that we are able to explain this. If you look at 115 Brigade, could you please describe those positions? What do those symbols and marks signify?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here, where it says "155," that's the command: The battalion commanders, the 2nd Battalion, 3rd Battalion. That's the disposition of the forces here in this area, facing Nedzarici, and here at the airport and Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of weapons do we see here?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see here that they have a 120-millimetre mortars, 82-millimetres, 62-millimetre. And a semi-circle behind this dot means that this is a platoon that has four weapons. And you can see here in the depth towards 101st Brigade in the city itself in the inhabited area, there were the barracks were, they are deep in the territory Nedzarici, Pale, Stup. They had their mortars deployed as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which means --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Let us now move north. 112th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please scroll down a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain those positions and the weapons?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here, again, we have mortars, and you have recoilless guns, anti-armour weapons, mortars. So we have several mortar positions here, here, here, and here. And here you have the anti-armour weapons, and recoilless guns that are used to fight armour. Just one suggestion. This means that this brigade was deployed around the city, and all the support artillery has to be in the depth. It cannot be at the front end of the defence because a mortar needs as four-man crew, and the crew would be engaged with infantry fire and it would be destroyed. The depth, that's the city, that's the depth where the depth of their defence was, and we could not target them there because we would hit the city centre. If you have combat, our artillery has to engage their firing positions to destroy their fire-power, and we didn't want to do that because we would have will to target the entire city.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And was this the situation throughout?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, the way that you see it here in this area and this is not our map. This is what they plotted. That's, I think, a map that was produced by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move north a little bit. If at least you can indicate to us what are those?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can you see here anti-aircraft, machine-gun, the command posts, this is a large calibre cannon here, mortars, mortars. So this all deployed in inhabited areas, and this is pretty far away from the front line, the front end. You can see it's maybe two or three kilometres in the depth of the defended territory in the inhabited areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now move east, and can you tell us what are those brigades and what kind of weapons are deployed there?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be 152nd, 105th Brigade. You see they have mortars. They have their command posts in the very city centre. All those flags that you see here, these are command posts in the most densely inhabited area. This is where 115th Brigade has its positions. This is -- this is where they deployed two mortar platoons in the most densely inhabited area of the city centre, and they put their firing points so deep inside their defended territory. And in order to target them, if we were to target them, we would have caused immense civilian casualties. That would have been a tragedy, and that's why we never did it. They exploited this fact to achieve their own successes. And they also used mobile mortar, mortars mounted on vehicles, and here at Cengic Vila you see that have both their command posts and mortar emplacements.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I almost failed to ask you that. When did they use those vehicle-mounted mortars, mobile mortars?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in 1992 and then on to 1995, at the beginning, they had few of such units, but then they intensified the manufacturing of those weapons at Zenica, at Vitez; and then they managed to bring it into the city, in particular mortars because they are easily transported through the tunnel. Of course, it is very difficult to bring in Howitzers or other weapons because they had to be dismantled first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what -- how -- where did they deploy those mobile mortars that they mounted on trucks?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they would -- you put some soil on the truck bed, you put the mortar up there, fire a few shells, and then you just move it. They would often provoke fire. They would provoke our response, and they wanted us to respond to return fire and then we would hit the area around the hospital where they would have put such mortars, but we did take great care.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you a document. There's just this one document left and then I would like to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DD00-3561. I don't know why it is so dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But could you please tell us what the date on this document is, whose document it is, and does it actually explain what it was that you talked about, how the in-depth positions were located along the front line that you spoke of until now?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date of this document of the BH army is the 16th of March, 1995, Command of the battalion of the Viteska Brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what is the order?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order says: "I order, I hereby order."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. Please. What does it say underneath the letterhead? What is this order for?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's this lot here: "Defence systems and engineering order."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. What kind of system?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it says so. It's written there, please.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't read it. Probably engineering support, combat system. Probably it says engineering support, combat system. I know about these things and that means --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. That will do. Would you look at the very end?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know, my document is clear, and why there are three's these black marks here. The English version is fine, but can it please be placed on the ELMO so that he have a proper look at it, so he can read the one but last paragraph, and so that he can read what is says on top of the document, because what it says there is ...

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I can see it this way, too. What paragraph do you want me to look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, remember what you couldn't read a few moments ago, at the very top, the letterhead.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The order on organising the firing system and the engineering support."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The one-but-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In all areas of defence, if you look at the PAMs and PATs, and you will" -- well, that means in the buildings and houses, that they should be built in depth, and that over their own heads they fire at our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document please be tendered, or rather, admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D194, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to what you saw in the map I showed you a few moments ago, where were all of their weapons?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see that they were all in the urban areas. It was all depicted in the map. We all saw that on the map what was marked in blue. You saw where machine-gun was, where a mortar was. You could see that it is throughout town, that these weapons are throughout town.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have to hurry. These are not all the weapons, the ones that are inscribed here?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if all the weapons were to be inscribed, it is just a small map, so it would just look like a big inkblot. You couldn't really see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One to 50.000 is the scale, so what is that if you look at such --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Can we just look at this other document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that would be my last question in relation to that document. The document is DD00-3318.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Look at this document, please. Could you look at the date, and could you tell me what it shows in relation to the firing positions that existed in depth as you told us? Can you just explain that, too?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we just see this a bit better. We cannot see the numbers properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You can see the date, can't you?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the date: The 13th of June, 1995. "Order". I cannot read this here. "Order to battalions: First of all" -- oh. This is -- well, "the first combat firing group consisting of" -- I cannot read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Look at the firing positions down there.

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, down there. "One in the region of Mojmilo, two in the region of the annex," that is near the Zeljeznicar football stadium, "with three plus one NB 82-millimetre mortar. Cengic Vila then," which is in the centre of town, "two mortars of 120-millimetre calibre," that is the biggest calibre. There is no bigger mortar calibre. "Then firing position five in the region of -- of the heating room of Cengic Vila, and then these 107-millimetre launchers in the area the hill of Mojmilo." Those are the ones that we did indicate that were involved in the preparation of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's not look at the entire document. It's three pages long. What does this mean when you look at this? Now, look, Cengic Vila and then it says the Bristol Hotel. So where were the firing positions within -- within the city zone itself?

utterances.speaker: STEVAN VELJOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, what it says here in the document was copied out on the map, because what is written in the document is copied out 90 per cent of it on the map, and we saw clearly what the map shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I would like to thank you for the time that you have given me to question the witness. I did have other matters to deal with, but this will be quite sufficient for you to learn some more about what it was that was happening at the time. Your Honours, sorry, this document, this document, could it please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D195, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Waespi, you have the night -- you have the night from which you can benefit and begin your cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 30th day of May, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.42 p.m.,
